summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with ongoing abdominal pain that worsened after eating, consistent with an acute on chronic flare. She had been on TPN since a recent admission but experienced increased pain after oral intake. Lipase and liver enzymes were normal, and MRCP showed chronic pancreatitis changes with stable pancreatic cysts, no acute inflammation. She remained on TPN and was managed with IV then oral pain medications, including an increase in her fentanyl patch to 100 mcg/hour. Pain improved with minimal oral intake. Iron deficiency anemia was confirmed with a ferritin of 9.8, and outpatient plans were made for colonoscopy and possible IV iron. Constipation, worsened by narcotics, was treated with increased bowel regimen. She was discharged home on TPN with visiting nurse services, follow-up arranged with GI, and instructions for repeat pancreatic imaging in 12 months.
